commits.message: Extract TokenBucket.consume() out of middleware/ratelimit.py into limiter/bucket.py
Wire RedisStore.incr_ttl() into Limiter.__init__ and drop the in-proc dict
Add fail-open path in Limiter.check() when RedisStore raises ConnErr; emit ratelimit_store_down metric
Tests for TokenBucket.consume(), RedisStore.incr_ttl() TTL rollover, and the fail-open branch

pull_requests.title: Move token-bucket rate limiting to a shared Redis store with a fail-open path
pull_requests.description: Refactors middleware/ratelimit.py: TokenBucket.consume() moves to limiter/bucket.py, and Limiter now reads its counter from RedisStore.incr_ttl() (INCR + EXPIRE in one round-trip) instead of a per-process dict, so the per-tenant RPS limit holds across all gateway instances. Limiter.check() gains a fail-open branch: on a RedisStore ConnErr it allows the request and emits the ratelimit_store_down metric rather than 500-ing the tenant. Closes #201.

review_comments.body: If RedisStore is down should check() fail open or fail closed?
Fail open, with the ratelimit_store_down metric so we can watch it. Failing closed would 500 every tenant on a blip.

linked_issues.title: Rate limit is per-instance, so the effective RPS is N times the configured limit
